---
title: "Learning Moment: Skill Defaults vs. Project Context"
date: 2026-06-19
categories: [claude, learning, ai-collaboration, claude-code, documentation, dotfiles, plan-review]
---

## Context

Setting up a new machine directory in a dotfiles repo.
The repo organizes everything by machine (`mac-laptop/`, `linux-laptop/`, etc.),
so each machine directory is self-contained.
Claude was following the brainstorming skill,
which instructs it to save design specs to `docs/superpowers/specs/` at the repo root.

## The Initial Ask

Claude was mid-brainstorming and reached the step where it writes the spec document.
It ran:

```bash
mkdir -p /path/to/dotfiles/docs/superpowers/specs
```

## Claude's Initial Response

Claude was following the skill's default path literally:
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` at the repo root.

## The Exchange

**Turn 1 — User:**

> i think the specs are specific to the system76 computer?
> should it go in that directory instead?
> why under overall docs in root?

**Turn 1 — Claude:**

Agreed immediately.
The spec describes a single machine's setup,
so it belongs inside that machine's directory, not at the repo root.
Redirected to `linux-laptop/docs/2026-06-19-<topic>-design.md`.

## The Final Solution

Specs for machine-specific work live inside the machine's own directory:
`linux-laptop/docs/`.
The brainstorming skill's default path (`docs/superpowers/specs/`) is appropriate
for project-wide specs but not for machine-specific ones.

## The Lesson

**What Claude got right:**
Following the skill's process — brainstorming, clarifying, writing a spec before building.
The workflow was correct.

**What required human expertise:**
Recognizing that the skill's default file location is a generic convention
that doesn't fit every project structure.
The repo's organizing principle (one directory per machine, each self-contained)
should override the skill's default.

**Why Claude missed it:**
Claude followed the skill instruction literally without asking
"does this convention fit the project I'm working in?"
Skill defaults are written for a generic project;
they don't automatically adapt to a specific repo's layout.

**Key takeaway:**
Skill defaults tell Claude *where to look*, not *what's right for this project* —
always ask whether the convention fits the project structure before accepting it.
